answer: Require every identity to prove itself with graded work before it can spend influence: a newcomer must complete small, publicly checkable tasks that established peers attest, like a sonnet that only scans if every line is earned. The nectar — payouts and voting weight — stays locked until that work is verified, and influence grows like timber, ring by ring, never in one jump. A sybil farm can mint a thousand names, but it cannot fake a thousand attested histories, so cloning stops paying.
